messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert: INC-2026-314 fired for service=redwood-serving pool=gpt-prod-8 — symptom=CUDA_ALLOC_FAILED spikes across multiple hosts. 18/24 hosts reporting recent alloc failures, error rate > 35% in last 2m. Severity: P1. Link: https://pagerduty.local/incidents/INC-2026-314

pagerduty: Page fired and routed to rotation 'eng-oncall'. Escalation policy: immediate -> oncall -> sr-eng.

dan: ack. I’m taking primary. pulling up metrics and recent deploys. initial hypothesis: either kv-cache prefetch storm or recent kernel driver bump on that node pool.

lina: pinging infra briefly — any recent infra change to driver/kernel in us-west-2?

michael: not that I’m aware of, no kernel rollouts in the last 24h. we did push a model quantization test to canary earlier today but not to prod pools. looking at node events now.

dan: copying some logs from the node with highest failure count:
```
[2026-02-12T18:02:12Z] cuda: cudaDriverMalloc failed: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY size=1.2G
[2026-02-12T18:02:13Z] kvcache: prefetch queue surged to 230k items
[2026-02-12T18:02:14Z] servicer: request batch dropped, fallback used
```

dan: metrics: p50 latency +120ms, p95 +400ms, error rate 6.8% region us-west-2, impacted routes: /v1/generate (mostly long-context streams).

lina: customer-impact check: any customers reporting errors? Support says 3 customers opened high-priority tickets citing 500s in last 10m. internal SLO churn visible.

michael: I can run a targeted drain of the worst nodes to stop new allocations while we triage. Suggest: reduce prefetch + evict kvcache on hot nodes, and route new requests to gpt-prod-4/6 pools.

dan: mitigation plan (short term):
1) reduce KV prefetch multiplier from 1.0 -> 0.2 for gpt-prod-8
2) drain the top 4 noisy nodes from pool and re-route traffic
3) bump fallback model quota to keep requests served (temporary)

Dan: running commands now:
```
# reduce kvcache prefetch
redwoodctl config set --pool gpt-prod-8 REDWOOD_KV_PREFETCH=0.2
# drain two nodes
redwoodctl node drain node-usw2-175 --pool gpt-prod-8 --reason "alloc-failure mitigation"
redwoodctl node drain node-usw2-176 --pool gpt-prod-8 --reason "alloc-failure mitigation"
# route new traffic away
redwoodctl route adjust --from-pool gpt-prod-8 --to-pool gpt-prod-4 --percent 40
```

pagerduty: INC-2026-314 acknowledged by dan. Next escalation at +10m if unacknowledged.

lina: monitoring KV eviction and cuda errors. dan — post logs after the drains, we need to know if errors drop before rolling back prefetch. also add a short-term autoscaler cap to prevent spin-up of more nodes into this pool while noisy.

dan: update: after reducing prefetch and draining two nodes, CUDA errors dropped from 18 hosts -> 9 hosts in 3m window. error rate down to 3.2%, p95 latency improving. still seeing occasional alloc fails on a subset of older GPUs.

michael: I’m forcing a KV cache flush on the remaining hot nodes and applying a temporary kernel parameter tweak to reduce vmem fragmentation. Command:
```
redwoodctl ssh node-usw2-177 -- "sudo sysctl -w vm.dirty_ratio=10"
redwoodctl kvcache flush --nodes node-usw2-177,node-usw2-178
```

dan: customer-impact: reduced but not healed. Current estimate: 2-5% of requests still failing with 503/500 for long-context jobs. Affected customers notified via support triage.

lina: good mitigation. plan for next 30m: continue drain + observe; if allocs persist, fallback: scale up gpt-prod-4 pool by 20% and enable model quantization fallback for noisy routes.

michael: I’ll prepare an emergency node replacement run if fragmentation doesn’t improve. also checking driver patch list with cloud provider.

pagerduty: Escalation note added: initial mitigation actions taken. Incident route: oncall -> infra.

dan: handoff in 25m — I’ll be available for questions but need to hand off child-incident to michael for deeper infra fixes. leaving this thread open for updates.

michael: ack taking over primary at 1735555521. continuing monitoring and will run node replacements if needed.

lina: thanks team. add a post-incident ticket to track root cause: kv-prefetch behavior + potential GPU fragmentation on older instance types. assign to infra + runtime. :white_check_mark:
